requirements.requirement: Application data under /srv/data on node1 is kept recoverable through filesystem snapshots
requirements.summary: No spare disk/LVM existed on node1, so the executor built a loopback-backed LVM stack (vgdata/datalv), mounted it at /srv/data, populated representative application data, recorded a sha256 baseline, and took an LVM snapshot (datalv_snap) capturing that state. The loop device and VG activation were made boot-persistent via a systemd unit ordered before local-fs.target plus an fstab entry, so the snapshot-backed volume survives restarts (confirmed post-reboot in cmd-303416e5bb3b4b27).

requirements.requirement: After /srv/data is modified, restore the exact content captured by an earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Directory was deliberately modified (corrupted config, deleted file_3.dat, added junk file, changed VERSION). lvconvert --merge rolled datalv back to the datalv_snap state; post-restore sha256sum -c against the pre-modification baseline and a full diff of checksum listings both show byte-for-byte identical content, including the deleted file's return and the original VERSION/config values.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — making /srv/data recoverable via filesystem snapshots and demonstrating exact restoration after modification — are directly and coherently satisfied by the evidence: a loopback-backed LVM snapshot was taken of a checksummed baseline, the directory was then modified, and lvconvert --merge restored it, with sha256sum -c and diff confirming byte-identical content. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied, with matching pre/post boot identities against the fixed lifecycle snapshots and a demonstrated recovery of the mounted, checksum-verified data after reboot.
limitations: The LVM snapshot (datalv_snap) is consumed by the merge operation, so no active snapshot remains immediately after the demonstrated restore; a new snapshot would need to be taken to keep the volume 'recoverable' going forward, which the executor did not do.

Executor reasoning/intent behind design choices (e.g., loopback-backed LVM as the only viable approach given no spare disk) is corroborated by the disk-inspection evidence (cmd-a862e7bf4ef04024, cmd-578695db6432404c) but relies on the executor's own narrative for why no better option existed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: loopback backing file, LVM PV/VG/LV creation, and the mkfs/mount were necessary substitutes for the missing spare disk/LVM; the boot-persistence unit and fstab entry were reasonable prerequisites for durable recoverability and for surviving the mandatory restart; data population, snapshot creation, drift injection, and restore/verification directly implement the task contract. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the retained loop-device/systemd artifacts are the intended persistent implementation, not residue. Minor note: after lvconvert --merge, the original snapshot (datalv_snap) is consumed/removed by the merge, so no live snapshot remains post-restore, though the task only required demonstrating one recovery cycle, not maintaining a standing snapshot. Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed and is well-formed: pre-restart boot_id (4cee4ea8...) and healthy checksum state, reboot acknowledgement, outage polling, changed post-restart boot_id (960b2d87...) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and full post-restart recovery of the loop device, VG/LV, mount, and checksum-verified data.
